en: Sutta Nipāta 5.6 Dhotaka-māṇava-pucchā “I ask you, Blessed One, tell me this:”
(Thus spoke the Venerable Dhotaka:
"O Great Seer, I long for your voice;
having heard your sound,"
“Train yourself for your own Nibbāna.
“Therefore, O Dhota,
exert yourself with diligence,” said the Blessed One.
Right here, being wise and mindful;
having heard this sound from here,
one should train for one's own Nibbāna.
“In the world of gods and humans,
I see a brahmin wandering about, possessing nothing.
To him, O All-Seeing One, I pay homage.”
“Release me from my doubts, Sakka!
“I will not allow anyone in the world, O Dhota, to release me from my state of doubt.”
“Fully understanding the Dhamma that is supreme,
you shall thus cross over this flood.
“O Brahmā, teach me out of compassion.”
May I understand the nature of discernment,
so that, like space, being untroubled,
I may dwell right here, peaceful and independent.”
“I shall proclaim peace to you,
Dhotaka,” said the Blessed One,
“a state visible in this very life, not based on hearsay.”
“Having understood that and practicing with mindfulness,
one crosses over attachment to the world.
“That indeed I rejoice in.”
The Great Seer [taught] supreme peace;
having understood this and practicing mindfully,
one crosses over attachment to the world.
“Whatever you perceive,
Dhotaṭṭha,” said the Blessed One,
“above, below, across, and in between;”
"Having understood this— that there is craving in the world for becoming and non-becoming— do not produce craving.
This is the fifth inquiry of the young brahmin Dhotaka.
